name: SHIDO permissionless V1-to-V2 migration arbitrage
summary: ShidoLock let anyone deposit a current V1 balance after the global unlock time and redeem the same token count of V2, without a holder snapshot, cutoff, cap, or value check. The attacker flash-bought cheap V1, immediately migrated it 1:1 into the more valuable V2 inventory, and sold the V2 into its WBNB pool.
notes: ShidoLock is a non-proxy direct contract. It first has code in its successful creation transaction at block 29347371; its 1,089-byte runtime hash is identical there and immediately before exploitation, and the exploit trace calls lockTokens and claimTokens directly without delegatecall.

The SHIDO/WBNB pair transferred exactly 1,016.085297305562276696 WBNB to the attacker helper in the exploit transaction. DefiLlama's nearest preceding BNB observation prices that gross victim-asset outflow at $248,758.00248634774. The helper repaid the separate 40 WBNB flash loan and sent 976.975297305562276696 WBNB to the attacker EOA; financing is not netted from gross loss. The onchain measurement replaces the seed row's $230,000 estimate.
